- **Alphabet and mass literacy** [`alphabet_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alphabet_writing.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Capitals and a cursive hand, words divided by points, no lower case. Many townsmen read notices and scratch graffiti. Schooling is private and paid; most country people cannot read.
- **Codex book and finding aids** [`codex_book`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/codex_book.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Books are papyrus rolls. Wax-tablet codices and parchment notebooks serve for drafts and accounts; Caesar sends despatches folded into pages. Nobody publishes literature that way. Local: Atticus' copyists; papyrus imported from Egypt; parchment (Pergamene skins).
- **Woodblock printing** [`woodblock_printing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/woodblock_printing.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Stamps on bricks, amphorae, lead pipes and seals are everyday; nobody inks one onto a page. Papyrus is ribbed and brittle, parchment dear, and slave copyists are cheap.
- **Movable-type printing press** [`printing_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/printing_press.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Mint die-cutters could cut punches, and lead and tin are plentiful. Missing are paper, an oil-based ink and the adjustable type mould. Presses work by lever and windlass. Local: die-engravers of the mint on the Arx.
- **Reproducing images (woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography)** [`lithography_engraving`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lithography_engraving.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Gem-cutters and die-engravers have the hand skill. Pictures in books are copied freehand and degrade with each copy. There is no paper to print on.
- **Relay post and public mail** [`postal_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/postal_system.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. No state post. Letters travel with one's own slave couriers (tabellarii), friends, or the tax companies' messengers. Caesar posts relay riders on campaign. Persian relays are known from Herodotus. Elsewhere: Ptolemaic Egypt, royal relay post; Han China, post stations.
- **Newspapers and periodicals** [`newspapers_periodicals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/newspapers_periodicals.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Since Caesar's consulship (59 BC) the doings of Senate and people are posted daily (acta diurna). Copies go to the provinces by private letter. Local: the Forum, where the acta are posted.
- **Scientific journal and peer review** [`scientific_journal`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_journal.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Greek scholars publish by letter and preface to a named colleague, as Archimedes did. No periodical, no printing.
- **Encyclopedias and dictionaries** [`encyclopedia_reference_works`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/encyclopedia_reference_works.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Varro's Antiquities (41 books; the part on religion dedicated to Caesar) is new, his De lingua Latina in progress. Cato's handbook for his son is old. Nothing is alphabetical. Local: M. Terentius Varro.
- **Library catalogue and classification** [`library_catalogue`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/library_catalogue.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Callimachus' Pinakes are the model. Roman libraries are private and arranged by Greek experts such as Tyrannion, with title tags glued to each roll. Local: Tyrannion of Amisus, grammarian in Rome; libraries of Atticus, Cicero, Varro and the Luculli. Elsewhere: Alexandria.
- **Pencil, steel pen and durable ink** [`pencil_steel_pen`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pencil_steel_pen.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Reed pen with soot-and-gum ink on papyrus, which sponges off; stylus on wax; a lead disc for ruling lines. No graphite, no iron-gall ink, no quill.
- **Shorthand (stenography)** [`shorthand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/shorthand.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Tiro, Cicero's freedman secretary, uses a system of signs; clerks took down Cato's Senate speech in 63 BC. Few are trained in it. Local: M. Tullius Tiro.
- **Typewriter** [`typewriter`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typewriter.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Copying documents (copying press, carbon paper, stencil duplicator)** [`copying_duplicating`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copying_duplicating.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. No paper. A room of slave copyists writing to dictation is the duplicator, and it is cheap.
- **Braille (tactile writing for blind people)** [`braille_tactile_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/braille_tactile_writing.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Raised dots on wood, lead sheet or wax are feasible at once. The blind learn by ear and have others read to them.
- **Sign languages of deaf people** [`sign_languages`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sign_languages.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Deaf people sign within their households. Formal contracts are spoken question and answer, so a deaf-mute cannot make them. Nobody teaches the deaf.
- **Knowledge in the vernacular; translation movements** [`vernacular_translation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vernacular_translation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Science and philosophy are Greek, read untranslated. Lucretius laments Latin's poverty; Cicero builds a Latin philosophical vocabulary in 45–44 BC. Mago's Punic farming manual was translated by Senate order. Local: Cicero; Varro.
- **Beacons, flag codes and heliograph** [`signal_beacons_flag_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/signal_beacons_flag_codes.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. The army uses trumpets, standards, fire and smoke. Polybius describes a torch code spelling letters from a five-by-five grid; no actual use of it is recorded.
- **Optical telegraph (semaphore network)** [`optical_telegraph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/optical_telegraph.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Polybius' torch alphabet is the idea, in a book. Without telescopes stations must stand close. The army and the grain supply would gain.
- **Standard time and time zones** [`standard_time_zones`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_time_zones.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low. Hours are twelfths of daylight, longer in summer. Each town reads its own sundial.
